key_insight: Near-duplicate pages that exact dedup misses can be stored as base-plus-delta behind a CXL controller, with LSH or MinHash picking the reference at write-back.
killer_doubt: Every P-page read needs 2 fetches (reference plus delta) plus decode. KSM, CoW KV sharing and BitDelta already capture most of the redundancy, so the marginal gain is likely <1.3x.
decisive_experiment: Snapshot memory of 3 production-like hosts (VM farm, forked workers, multi-variant LLM server). Measure what XOR/byte-delta adds beyond KSM plus zstd, then simulate the 2-fetch latency in a CXL model.
prior_art: Difference Engine (Gupta et al., OSDI 2008) sub-page patching of similar pages; Thesaurus (ASPLOS 2020) LSH base+diff; KSM; vLLM copy-on-write beam KV.

key_insight: One resident base plus 1-bit sign deltas with per-row scales, fused into the GEMM, cuts the memory of each extra full fine-tune to ~1/16 of a copy.
killer_doubt: This is BitDelta exactly, already open source. Multi-tenant full fine-tunes are a few % of inference memory, and LoRA covers most variants, so the gain over current practice is ~1x.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. At most, benchmark 100 tenants of an 8B model with BitDelta against multi-LoRA: HBM per tenant, tokens/s and quality.
prior_art: BitDelta (Liu et al. 2024); DeltaZip; Delta-CoMe; S-LoRA, Punica and vLLM multi-LoRA. Same as R28 I-10409 (DROP).

key_insight: Variants derived from other variants (base to instruct to domain to customer) could share deltas hierarchically, so each level stores only what changed from its parent.
killer_doubt: Most fine-tunes fork from one base (depth ~1), which is just BitDelta. At depth k, 1-bit errors compound and the epilogue adds k delta passes; depth >2 likely loses quality.
decisive_experiment: From a public model tree (base, instruct, 10 domain children, 50 grandchildren), compare chained 1-bit deltas with flat-from-base deltas: perplexity drift by depth and decode tokens/s.
prior_art: BitDelta, DeltaZip, Delta-CoMe, ComPEFT; Hugging Face model-tree lineage metadata. No hierarchical-delta serving found [training knowledge].

key_insight: Trained per-type dictionaries let small records (log lines, JSON) compress 5-10x where generic LZ fails, and a near-memory decoder hides the cost.
killer_doubt: Log and JSON stores already compress in software (columnar stores, CLP, zstd dictionaries) and hold only a few % of fleet DRAM, so the world-level DRAM saving is <<10%.
decisive_experiment: Replay one log-analytics and one document-store workload. Compare DRAM per GB ingested for software zstd-dictionary compression against an emulated CXL hardware decompressor at equal query latency.
prior_art: zstd trained dictionaries (Meta); Intel IAA/QAT; IBM z15 on-chip compression; Marvell Structera inline-LZ4 CXL; YScope CLP log compression.

key_insight: Shared prefixes (system prompts, tool schemas, documents) make KV highly redundant across users, so a content-addressed flash tier avoids both recompute and HBM pinning.
killer_doubt: Already deployed in production by Moonshot (Mooncake), DeepSeek (disk context cache) and the LMCache and vLLM ecosystem, so the marginal gain over the state of the art is ~1x.
decisive_experiment: None needed. If anything, quantify which share of fleet KV is prefix-shareable across tenants on a public multi-tenant trace.
prior_art: Mooncake (Kimi); LMCache; CachedAttention (USENIX ATC 2024); DeepSeek on-disk context caching (3FS); vLLM and SGLang prefix caching.

key_insight: Platform floors (Copilot+ PC 16 GB) and phones' 'virtual RAM' claims already steer DRAM content unaudited. An audited effective-GB metric could let specs and procurement count OS compression.
killer_doubt: macOS, Windows and Android already compress memory silently (~1.2-1.5x effective), so certification adds no capacity. It saves bits only if spec owners lower floors, worth perhaps ~1% of world bits.
decisive_experiment: Build an open trace-replay suite (browser tabs, Office, Teams, IDE) scoring QoS at 8, 12 and 16 GB on three OSes, then pilot it with one large procurement buyer and one platform-spec owner. About $300k.
prior_art: None found for an audited effective-memory rating. Related: SPEC and BAPCo benchmarks, Apple's contested '8 GB Mac' claim, phone RAM-extension marketing [training knowledge].

key_insight: For in-memory data that genuinely is replicated, RS(k,m) striping cuts redundancy from 3x to ~1.25x with line-rate NIC coding.
killer_doubt: Most in-memory caches are not replicated, since misses fall back to the database. Where they are, EC-Cache, Hydra and Carbink already ship this; world DRAM saving <2%.
decisive_experiment: None needed for novelty. At most, survey how much fleet DRAM sits in triple-replicated in-memory stores, using public hyperscaler workload papers.
prior_art: EC-Cache (OSDI 2016); Cocytus (FAST 2016); Hydra (FAST 2022); Carbink (OSDI 2022, Google); Intel ISA-L and SmartNIC erasure-coding offload.

key_insight: Codebook index assignment gives redundancy-free error protection: flips land on neighbouring codewords. Weights, the largest static inference tenant, can then sit ECC-free in relaxed-refresh or reject cells.
killer_doubt: At 1% BER, 15% of 16-bit AQLM indices flip, with only 16 Hamming neighbours per codeword. Distortion may fall 2-3x, not 5-10x. Real retention errors are asymmetric and clustered.
decisive_experiment: Anneal index orders for AQLM, VPTQ and QuIP# codebooks on Llama-8B/70B, then inject iid, asymmetric and row-clustered 1e-3 to 1e-2 flips. Compare perplexity and MMLU with random-order and int3-with-protected-scales baselines. GPU weeks, under $50k.
prior_art: Pseudo-Gray coding (Zeger-Gersho) and channel-optimized VQ (Farvardin) for speech; EDEN (MICRO 2019) approximate DRAM. No faulty-memory application to weight VQ found (via search snippet).

key_insight: A relaxed-spec 'AI-grade' SKU behind a long-codeword CXL controller turns retention-failing dies and marginal process windows into bits. AI tensors are read in multi-KB blocks, which amortizes page-level LDPC.
killer_doubt: Mature-node rejects are a few % and already resold (Micron SpecTek). Ramp fallout (HBM, 1c) is mostly stack, TSV or hard defects; added supply likely 2-8%, not 5-15%.
decisive_experiment: Buy 200 DDR5 reject or downbinned dies (or run standard DIMMs hot at 10-50x tREFI) and map error clustering on an FPGA tester. Then measure the BER and burst profile that a 4 KB LDPC with interleaving clears.
prior_art: Micron SpecTek downgraded parts; ArchShield (ISCA 2013); X-PPR recycled-DRAM CXL repair (2025). In-study twin: R21 I-01312 (ADVANCE) and R26 I-05038. Fold into I-01312.

key_insight: KV lives seconds to minutes and can be rebuilt by re-prefill, so it fits low-refresh cells naturally. int4 with protected scales already bounds flip magnitude, and clamping caps the residual.
killer_doubt: At 1% BER, ~4% of int4 KV elements are corrupted. Clamping adds little beyond int4's own bound; it hinges on unmeasured attention tolerance, and perplexity loss >0.3 kills it.
decisive_experiment: Run the same fault-injection harness as I-10421 on int4 KV (Llama-8B, RULER and LongBench), with and without clamping and softmax capping, at 1e-3 to 1e-2 BER and with asymmetric decay. Under $30k.
prior_art: Ranger range restriction (Chen et al., DSN 2021); FT-ClipAct (2020); EDEN (MICRO 2019); KIVI and KVQuant int2-4 KV quantization.

key_insight: Training under stochastic eviction could teach models to carry facts forward redundantly. Random Attention (2026) shows reasoning traces already tolerate random eviction, and the fragile part is the prompt.
killer_doubt: MLA, GQA and DMC already cut KV 4-14x architecturally, and no training recovers an evicted needle. The residual gain over the 2026 state of the art may be <1.5x.
decisive_experiment: Continue pretraining a 1B model on 2-5B tokens with 30-70% biased stochastic eviction. Compare RULER and needle retrieval at 2-4x smaller KV budgets against SnapKV and Random Attention on the untouched model. About $50-100k of compute.
prior_art: DMC (Nawrot et al., ICML 2024) trained KV compression; Locret retaining heads; DeepSeek MLA and NSA; Random Attention inference-time eviction (arXiv 2609.03430, via search snippet).

key_insight: Clean, refetchable data needs only error detection plus a cheap refetch, so a code can be tuned for throughput rather than a 1e-15 frame-error guarantee.
killer_doubt: At 4 KB, 1% BER, the ML bound needs ~10.9% parity at FER 1e-6 versus ~12.3% at 1e-15: ~1.5 points saved, not half. 64 B reads decode 4 KB.
decisive_experiment: None needed beyond the finite-length bound computed above. Fold the refetch fallback into the I-10425 / R21 I-01312 controller as a policy for clean pages.
prior_art: Heterogeneous-Reliability Memory (Luo et al., DSN 2014) recovers clean pages from storage; Linux hwpoison clean-page drop; in-study R17 I-02525 (DROP) and R28 I-10420 (HOLD).
